panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: X-ray of hand/wrist showing generalized osteopenia and tubulation deformities (irregular epiphyses) in phalanges consistent with Wolcott-Rallison Syndrome. B: Chest X-ray showing generalized skeletal osteopenia as part of the survey for Wolcott-Rallison Syndrome. C: X-ray of knees/legs showing epiphyseal dysplasia in distal femur/proximal tibia and generalized osteopenia. D: Lateral spine X-ray showing generalized osteopenia as part of the survey for Wolcott-Rallison Syndrome.

in_text_mentions: At a routine visit at the age of 3 years and 5 months, her height was 90.9 cm (-1.53 standard deviation score) and weight was 11.3 kg (-2.45 standard deviation score). Her HbA1c was 8.69% while taking insulin detemir once a day and insulin lispro three times a day, with a total daily dose of insulin of 1.2 UI/kg. An X-ray survey showed osteopenia, generalized (proximal tibia, distal femur, and proximal phalanges) epiphyseal dysplasia, and tubulation deformities in the carpal bones and phalanges, but there were no abnormal findings in vertebral and pelvic bones (Figure 1).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Lateral thoracolumbar spine radiograph of a pediatric Wolcott-Rallison syndrome patient, showing classic skeletal manifestations of the disease including captioned generalized osteopenia, with additional proposed findings of vertebral beaking consistent with reported skeletal dysplasia. B: Anteroposterior lumbosacral and pelvic radiograph of the same pediatric Wolcott-Rallison syndrome patient, demonstrating captioned generalized osteopenia, with proposed findings of spina bifida occulta at L5 and vertebral beaking consistent with reported skeletal abnormalities. C: Hand radiograph of the same pediatric Wolcott-Rallison syndrome patient, showing classic epiphyseal dysplasia (consistent with cone-shaped phalangeal epiphyses) and generalized osteopenia as reported in the figure caption, representing characteristic skeletal manifestations of the disease.

in_text_mentions: nd extension limitation in all joints (Figure 1). Height was severely retarded (102.6 cm, height SD score: -3.6). Growth velocity was 2 cm per year despite his better metabolic control. X-rays revealed beaking of both thoracic and lumbar vertebrae, spina bifida at L5 vertebrae and generalized epiphyseal-metaphyseal dysplasia (Figure 2). Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DEXA) showed osteopenia according to height-age (L2-4 Z-score: -1.6), and abdominal ultrasonography revealed hypoplasia of the pancreas (severely atrophic). Cerebellar atrophy was detected on cranial magnetic resonance imaging.

plate_findings.evidence: Short and broad metacarpi and phalanges

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Hand X-ray (Panel A) of a pediatric WRS patient demonstrating characteristic skeletal dysplasia including shortened/broad metacarpals and phalanges, and porotic (osteopenic) bones, consistent with the article's description of spondylo-epiphyseal dysplasia. B: Chest-humeri X-ray (Panel B) showing broadened epiphyses of the humeri, a manifestation of spondylo-epiphyseal dysplasia in Wolcott-Rallison syndrome.
panels.attribution_text: Sümegi et al. A novel splice site indel alteration in the EIF2AK3 gene is responsible for the first cases of Wolcott-Rallison syndrome in Hungary.. BMC medical genetics 2020. doi:10.1186/s12881-020-0985-6. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Characteristic signs of spondylo-epiphyseal dysplasia on chest-humeri and arm X-rays. Hand (a) and Chest-humeri (b) X-rays of Patient 1 are presented. Short and broad metacarpi and phalanges, porotic bones, hypoplastic bony islands of the basal phalanges below the epiphyseal plates are clearly visible. The epiphyses of the humeri are broadened, the vertebrae have normal morphology
